title: Wearable-based health age models for cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic risk profiling and coaching
summary: A coachable health-age metric built from wearable signals predicted hypertension, cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes over eight years in All of Us (n = 22,748), and a world model pre-trained on about 2.28 million Fitbit person-weeks forecast 12-week responses to habit changes. In a blinded comparison, coaches preferred the counterfactual-grounded plans in 71.4% of 490 paired reviews, and physicians rated 97.6% of physiological claims accurate. The authors state that all evaluations were offline on retrospective cohorts, that the models are research prototypes, not clinical tools, and that prospective trials are needed.
ai_technology: Coachable health-age model, SensorWM action-conditioned world model, feasibility-constrained optimizer with a language model agent, multimodal CKM deviation model

evidence.tested: Retrospective prediction in All of Us (n = 22,748) and WEAR-ME (n = 819), a longitudinal Fitbit cohort (n = 1,464), and a blinded review of 49 coaching profiles by 5 coaches and 5 physicians (490 paired reviews).
evidence.unknown: Prospective effect on habit change or long-term health not tested; authors say prospective trials are needed. The language model used for coaching text is not named in the source.
evidence.ai_role: Built the health-age metric and multimodal CKM model from wearable and clinical markers, forecast physiological responses to habit changes with a world model, and filtered and converted simulated habit plans into coaching text with a language model agent.
